doc: The burst filter: finding bursts in a photon stream and reading their properties. find_bursts returns an (n_bursts, 2) block of start/stop indices and get_all_burst_properties an (n_bursts, 5) block of per-burst numbers -- both 2-D outputs, which is where the four bindings differ most: Python and JavaScript carry the shape, R hands back a column-major array with a dim attribute, and Java has no 2-D output typemap at all and reads a nested vector proxy row by row.

cases.doc: The default burst search over the reference file. The ranges are start/stop pairs, so the block has two columns and an even length.

Five properties per burst. The first row is pinned element by element, which is the check that catches a transposed or column-major read -- the values have different magnitudes, so a wrong orientation cannot pass by coincidence.
